newsitem.title: UK: NWE gasoline ends higher, arbritrage divides opini.
newsitem.headline: NWE gasoline ends higher, arbritrage divides opini.

text.p: NWE gasoline prices ended modestly higher on Thursday but traders were divided over the market's next move primarily because of high freight rates and the arbitrage.
"It looks very strong," said one trader. "I think (the arb) is closed by about $2 for ARA material but that won't impede anyone from shipping...A lot has (already) gone to the States."
But another said the arbitrage was shut and unless NWE prices retreat, more supplies will be stuck in the local market.
"Gasoline seems to be quite strong if you look historically at the crack (spread) and with the arb virtually closed,.
"The States has to move up or Europe down," he said.
Eurograde barges ended $3 higher at $220/$222 fob ARA, with the last trades heard at $220. Regular unleaded was quieter, notionally ending up $4 at $212/$214.
Gasoline inventories held in independent tankage in the Amsterdam-Rotterdam-Antwerp area, industry sources said, rose to 525,000 tonnes as of January 23, up from 475,000-500,000 the previous week.
Incoming barges and coasters outweighed departing cargo loads to NWE and across the Atlantic and barges leaving for Germany, they said. Activity was brisk.

Stichting Euroilstock said in its monthly report on Thursday that gasoline production in the European Union, excluding Sweden, fell 2.2 percent in December to 3.223 million bpd, unchanged from a year ago.
The high freight rates also stymined trade in the Med, where demand from eastern destinations and from the U.S. buoyed prices.
"The arb is still open," from the Med to the U.S., said one local trader. "It's just that there are no ships."
